sentences.text:
Ashok Agarwal vs The State Of West Bengal & Anr on 14 June,
2022

14.06. 2022 item No.44 n.b.
ct. no. 34 Crr 1922 of 2022 Ashok Agarwal Vs. The State of West Bengal & Anr.
Mr. Souvik Mitter, Mr. Rajdeep Mazumdar, Mr. Santanu Chatterjee, Mr. Moyukh Mukherjee, .....for
the Petitioner
The present revisional application has been preferred challenging the order of the Appellate Court dated 31.5. 2022.

Records reflect that the present petitioner was convicted and sentenced by the Learned Senior Municipal Magistrate, Calcutta in connection with Case No.1D/08 for suffering simple imprisonment for six months and to pay of fine of Rs.5,000/ i.d. S.I. for one month under Section 16(1)a(i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act.
In view of the subject matter of the present revisional application involving questions of fact and law, I am of the opinion that the records are required to be placed before this Court.
Accordingly, the department is directed to place the records of both the Courts i.e. the Learned Senior Municipal Magistrate as well as the Learned Appellate Court.

The petitioner is directed to serve a copy of the revisional application upon the opposite party no.1 through the office of the Learned Public Prosecutor, High Court, Calcutta and upon the opposite party no. 2 both at its official address also by Speed Post with acknowledgment due and file affidavit of service on the next date fixed for hearing.

List the matter under the heading "Contested Application"
on August 11, 2022.
The petitioner shall continue on the same bail and bond granted by the Learned Appellate Court/Trial Court till further hearing of the case.
The Learned Senior Municipal Magistrate is directed to act on the server copy of this order downloaded from the official website of this Hon'ble High Court.
All pending connected applications, if any, are consequently disposed of.
